---
title: "NDVI: Measuring Vegetation from Two Bands"
date: 2026-09-07
categories: [tool, raster, bilingual]
description: "Compute the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index from a Red and a near-infrared band, and see it as a colored map — in Python and R on the same map."
---

Plants reflect near-infrared (NIR) light strongly and absorb most red
light for photosynthesis — a signature no bare soil, water, or
built surface shares. The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index,
NDVI, turns that one physical fact into a single number per pixel:

$$\text{NDVI} = \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{Red}}{\text{NIR} + \text{Red}}$$

Same formula as [Raster Band Math](raster-band-math.qmd)'s Normalized
Difference operator — this article fixes it to a specific pair of
bands and gives the result a name, a conventional range, and a
color scheme, because that's what turns "a computed raster" into
"a vegetation map."

Just want the map, without the rest of the reading? Use the
[standalone tool](/tools/ndvi-calculator.html) — same engine, pick
your bands directly.

## 2. Why NDVI, and its most common real-world mistake

Three things worth knowing before the first computed map:

- **It's bounded, by construction.** Normalizing by `NIR + Red`
  (rather than a plain difference) squeezes the result into roughly
  `-1..1` regardless of the sensor's raw value range — a Landsat scene
  in reflectance units and a raw-DN Sentinel-2 tile produce NDVI on
  the *same* scale, which is exactly why a fixed color scale (not a
  per-file min/max) makes sense here, unlike the generic Band Math
  tool.
- **Roughly**: negative values are usually water, values near zero
  are bare soil or built surfaces, and increasingly positive values
  track increasingly dense, healthy vegetation. "Roughly" is doing
  real work in that sentence — season, sensor, and atmospheric
  correction all shift the exact thresholds; treat it as a ranking,
  not a lab measurement.
- **The single most common real-world mistake: Red and NIR swapped,
  or the wrong band picked entirely.** A GeoTIFF's band order isn't
  standardized — it's whatever the sensor or processing pipeline put
  there, and the file itself never declares "band 4 is Red." Swap the
  two bands and NDVI doesn't error, it just silently inverts —
  vegetation reads as water-like and vice versa, a wrong answer that
  *looks* like a plausible map. Worth a specific check (`0.2 <= NDVI
  <= 0.9` somewhere near obvious vegetation in the image) before
  trusting a result on an unfamiliar file, not just a general
  disclaimer to keep in mind.

```{ojs}
  await map.ready();
  return map;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```

```{ojs}
FOOTPRINT_PAINT = ({
  "fill-color": "#42583c",
  "fill-opacity": 0.35,
  "fill-outline-color": "#2a2117"
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Brown (bare soil/water) -> pale yellow (sparse) -> green (dense
// vegetation) -- the conventional NDVI palette, deliberately
// different from the generic viridis ramp Raster Band Math uses
// (WebGeoDS.Map.DEFAULT_RASTER_RAMP) since a domain-specific tool
// should look like one. Same 5-stop [t, r, g, b] shape, t mapping
// onto the fixed -1..1 scale below.
NDVI_RAMP = [
  [0.00, 140, 90, 45],
  [0.30, 210, 190, 130],
  [0.50, 230, 220, 140],
  [0.75, 130, 190, 80],
  [1.00, 20, 90, 30]
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
base64ToBytes = (base64Str) => {
  const binary = atob(base64Str);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Same reasoning as the other bilingual raster articles: separate
// mutable state so Reset can clear the cards even though there's
// nothing to re-run.
mutable pyResult = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable rResult = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
pyCompute = WebGeoDS.getCellValue("ndvi-py", Generators)
{
  if (pyCompute && pyCompute.summary) {
    const s = pyCompute.summary;
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("ndvi-py-footprint", pyCompute.footprint, { paint: FOOTPRINT_PAINT });
    await sharedMap.fitToData(pyCompute.footprint);
    if (s.min !== null) {
      // Fixed -1..1 scale, not this result's own min/max -- see
      // section 2's note on why NDVI gets a fixed reference scale.
      await sharedMap.setRasterImage("ndvi-py-result", {
        bounds: s.wgs84Bounds,
        width: s.width,
        height: s.height,
        values: new Float32Array(base64ToBytes(s.data).buffer),
        min: -1,
        max: 1,
        colorRamp: NDVI_RAMP
      });
    }
    mutable pyResult = s;
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
statCard = (label, s) => {
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.style.flex = "1";

  const heading = document.createElement("div");
  heading.className = "webgeods-label";
  heading.textContent = label;

  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "webgeods-stat-grid";
  wrap.appendChild(box);

  const row = (rowLabel, value) => {
    const dt = document.createElement("div");
    dt.className = "webgeods-stat-label";
    dt.textContent = rowLabel;
    const dd = document.createElement("div");
    dd.className = "webgeods-stat-value";
    dd.textContent = value;
    box.append(dt, dd);
  };

  if (!s) {
    row("NDVI", "—");
    return wrap;
  }

  row("Dimensions", `${s.width} × ${s.height} px`);
  row("CRS", s.crs === null || s.crs === undefined ? `Unknown ⚠️ ${s.crsWarning}` : s.crs);
  if (s.displayCrsAssumption) {
    row("Display assumption", `${s.displayCrsAssumption} — map only, not a fact about the file`);
  }
  row("NDVI range (this file)", s.min !== null ? `${s.min} to ${s.max} (mean ${s.mean})` : "all NoData");
  row("NoData pixels", `${s.nodataCount.toLocaleString()} / ${s.totalPixels.toLocaleString()}`);

  return wrap;
}
```

## 4. Compute: run NDVI in Python or R

Run the same computation on the current data (your file uploaded
above, or the built-in example below) — edit `band_red`/`band_nir`
to match your file (common conventions: Landsat 8/9 Red=band 4,
NIR=band 5; Sentinel-2 Red=band 4, NIR=band 8 — but always confirm
against the file at hand, not just the sensor name) and re-run.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Python

```{.webgeods-python #ndvi-py}
#| package: rasterio, numpy
import base64
import rasterio
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
from rasterio.io import MemoryFile
from rasterio.warp import transform_bounds
import numpy as np

path = None
for candidate in ["/uploaded.tif"]:
    try:
        with rasterio.open(candidate):
            path = candidate
            break
    except Exception:
        pass

# No file uploaded yet: a synthetic Red/NIR pair shaped like a real
# vegetation signature (NIR up, Red down where "vegetation" is
# present) rather than two arbitrary bands -- see section 2.
memfile = None
if path is None:
    n = 20
    xs = np.arange(n)
    ys = np.arange(n)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    vegetation = np.exp(-((X - 10) ** 2 + (Y - 10) ** 2) / 30)
    red_band = (0.25 - 0.20 * vegetation).astype("float32")
    nir_band = (0.10 + 0.50 * vegetation).astype("float32")
    red_band[0, 0] = -9999
    nir_band[0, 0] = -9999
    transform = from_origin(12.40, 41.95, 0.005, 0.005)
    memfile = MemoryFile()
    with memfile.open(
        driver="GTiff", height=n, width=n, count=2,
        dtype="float32", crs="EPSG:4326", transform=transform, nodata=-9999
    ) as dst:
        dst.write(red_band, 1)
        dst.write(nir_band, 2)
    path = memfile.name

band_red = 1
band_nir = 2

with rasterio.open(path) as src:
    red = src.read(band_red, masked=True).astype("float32").filled(np.nan)
    nir = src.read(band_nir, masked=True).astype("float32").filled(np.nan)

    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        result = (nir - red) / (nir + red)

    # Inf/NaN (from an all-zero pixel pair) folded into NoData the
    # same way as every other raster tool on this site.
    result[~np.isfinite(result)] = np.nan

    valid = result[np.isfinite(result)]
    has_valid = valid.size > 0

    crs_warning = None
    display_crs_assumption = None
    if src.crs is not None:
        crs_for_transform = src.crs
        crs_label = str(src.crs)
    else:
        crs_for_transform = "EPSG:4326"
        crs_label = None
        crs_warning = "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
        display_crs_assumption = "EPSG:4326"

    try:
        wgs84_bounds = transform_bounds(crs_for_transform, "EPSG:4326", *src.bounds)
    except Exception:
        wgs84_bounds = src.bounds

    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = wgs84_bounds
    footprint = {
        "type": "FeatureCollection",
        "features": [{
            "type": "Feature",
            "properties": {"name": "NDVI footprint"},
            "geometry": {
                "type": "Polygon",
                "coordinates": [[[minx, miny], [maxx, miny], [maxx, maxy], [minx, maxy], [minx, miny]]]
            }
        }]
    }

    data_b64 = base64.b64encode(result.astype("float32").tobytes()).decode("ascii")

    summary = {
        "width": src.width,
        "height": src.height,
        "data": data_b64,
        "wgs84Bounds": [round(float(v), 6) for v in wgs84_bounds],
        "crs": crs_label,
        "crsWarning": crs_warning,
        "displayCrsAssumption": display_crs_assumption,
        "min": round(float(valid.min()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        "max": round(float(valid.max()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        "mean": round(float(valid.mean()), 4) if has_valid else None,
        "nodataCount": int(result.size - valid.size),
        "totalPixels": int(result.size),
    }

if memfile is not None:
    memfile.close()

{
    "summary": summary,
    "footprint": footprint
}
```

## R

```{.webgeods-r #ndvi-r}
#| package: terra, jsonlite, codetools
library(terra)

path <- NULL
for (candidate in c("/uploaded.tif")) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ rast(candidate); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) { path <- candidate; break }
}

if (is.null(path)) {
  # Same synthetic Red/NIR pair as the Python fallback.
  n <- 20
  xs <- 0:(n - 1)
  ys <- 0:(n - 1)
  vegetation <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) exp(-((x - 10)^2 + (y - 10)^2) / 30))
  red_band <- 0.25 - 0.20 * vegetation
  nir_band <- 0.10 + 0.50 * vegetation
  red_band[1, 1] <- NA
  nir_band[1, 1] <- NA
  r <- c(
    rast(red_band, crs = "EPSG:4326"),
    rast(nir_band, crs = "EPSG:4326")
  )
  ext(r) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.005, 41.95 - n * 0.005, 41.95)
} else {
  r <- rast(path)
}

band_red <- 1
band_nir <- 2

red <- r[[band_red]]
nir <- r[[band_nir]]

result <- (nir - red) / (nir + red)

# ifel() is terra's own vectorized if/else -- same reasoning as
# raster-band-math.qmd's use of it for Inf/NaN cleanup after a
# division.
result <- ifel(is.finite(result), result, NA)

was_missing_crs <- crs(r) == ""
crs_warning <- NULL
display_crs_assumption <- NULL
if (was_missing_crs) {
  crs_warning <- "No CRS declared — spatial location cannot be reliably interpreted."
  display_crs_assumption <- "EPSG:4326"
  crs(r) <- "EPSG:4326"
}
crs_label <- if (was_missing_crs) {
  NULL
} else {
  crs_desc <- crs(r, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(r, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

e <- ext(r)
bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, ", ", e$xmax, " ", e$ymin, ", ",
  e$xmax, " ", e$ymax, ", ", e$xmin, " ", e$ymax, ", ",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(r))
bbox_wgs84 <- tryCatch(project(bbox_vect, "EPSG:4326"), error = function(err) bbox_vect)
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_wgs84)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))
e_wgs84 <- ext(bbox_wgs84)

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("NDVI footprint")),
    geometry = list(
      type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"),
      coordinates = list(footprint_coords)
    )
  ))
)

vals <- values(result, mat = FALSE)
valid <- vals[is.finite(vals)]
has_valid <- length(valid) > 0

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(as.numeric(ifelse(is.finite(vals), vals, NaN)), con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
data_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

# jsonlite::toJSON() treats every length-1 vector as a single-element
# array by default — a genuine scalar (a width, a CRS string) needs an
# explicit jsonlite::unbox() to serialize as one. ub()/ub_if() below
# are just that, plus a NULL passthrough for optional fields (see
# geospatial-file-inspection.qmd for the full reasoning on why this,
# not toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE), is the safer default).
ub <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(x)
ub_if <- function(cond, x) if (cond) jsonlite::unbox(x) else NULL

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)),
  height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)),
  data = jsonlite::unbox(data_b64),
  wgs84Bounds = round(c(e_wgs84$xmin, e_wgs84$ymin, e_wgs84$xmax, e_wgs84$ymax), 6),
  crs = ub(crs_label),
  crsWarning = ub(crs_warning),
  displayCrsAssumption = ub(display_crs_assumption),
  min = ub_if(has_valid, round(min(valid), 4)),
  max = ub_if(has_valid, round(max(valid), 4)),
  mean = ub_if(has_valid, round(mean(valid), 4)),
  nodataCount = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals) - length(valid)),
  totalPixels = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals))
)

result_out <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

:::

## 5. Same spatial question, two languages

Same divergence already documented in
[Raster Band Math](raster-band-math.qmd#same-spatial-question-two-languages)
— numpy needs an explicit `np.errstate` context to suppress the
runtime warning a division by zero would otherwise print, while
terra's `ifel()` is a single vectorized call with no equivalent
warning. Nothing about NDVI specifically changes that comparison; the
formula is just a Normalized Difference with the bands fixed to
Red/NIR.

## 6. A raster with no declared CRS

Same convention as every other Raster tool on this site — a missing
CRS shows "Unknown" plus a separate "Display assumption" row, never
silently relabeled as WGS84. NDVI itself doesn't change based on
CRS — the arithmetic is per-pixel regardless of where the pixel sits
on the earth — but the footprint on the map still needs *some*
projection to draw.[^ndvi-crs-missing]

[^ndvi-crs-missing]: The reusable cell pair above already builds the
synthetic Red/NIR pair whenever nothing has been uploaded — click
**▶ Run** on both languages in section 4 to see it with a real CRS.
This button swaps in the same pair, minus the CRS.


```{ojs}

e <- ext(r)
bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, ", ", e$xmax, " ", e$ymin, ", ",
  e$xmax, " ", e$ymax, ", ", e$xmin, " ", e$ymax, ", ",
  e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(r))
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_vect)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("NDVI footprint")),
    geometry = list(type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"), coordinates = list(footprint_coords))
  ))
)

vals <- values(result, mat = FALSE)
valid <- vals[is.finite(vals)]
has_valid <- length(valid) > 0

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(as.numeric(ifelse(is.finite(vals), vals, NaN)), con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
data_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)), height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)), data = jsonlite::unbox(data_b64),
  wgs84Bounds = round(c(e$xmin, e$ymin, e$xmax, e$ymax), 6),
  crs = NULL, crsWarning = jsonlite::unbox(crs_warning),
  displayCrsAssumption = jsonlite::unbox(display_crs_assumption),
  min = if (has_valid) jsonlite::unbox(round(min(valid), 4)) else NULL,
  max = if (has_valid) jsonlite::unbox(round(max(valid), 4)) else NULL,
  mean = if (has_valid) jsonlite::unbox(round(mean(valid), 4)) else NULL,
  nodataCount = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals) - length(valid)), totalPixels = jsonlite::unbox(length(vals))
)

result_out <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)`
```

## 7. Where to next

- **Just needed the map?** The
  [standalone NDVI Calculator](/tools/ndvi-calculator.html) picks Red
  and NIR from a dropdown, no editing required.
- **Different two bands, or a different operation?**
  [Raster Band Math](raster-band-math.qmd) is the general version of
  this same computation — add/subtract/multiply/divide, any two
  bands, no vegetation assumption.
- **Not sure what's in the file yet?** Start with
  [Raster Inspector](/tools/raster-inspector.html) — dimensions,
  bands, CRS, NoData, before computing anything.
- **Working with terrain instead of imagery?** See
  [Viewshed](raster-viewshed.qmd) — what's visible from a point,
  accounting for the ground in between.
